title: Analysis of erratic breathing patterns during cardiopulomnary excersise testing: A comparison between post-COVID patients and endurance trained controls
summary:
The post-COVID syndrome is associated with persistent symptoms such as exertional dyspnoea, reduced physical performance and cognitive impairments. Dysfunctional or erratic breathing patterns are being discussed as a possible cause. These can be observed during cardiopulomnary excersise testing; however, erratic breathing have predominantly been assessed subjectively based on visual evaluation of the V’T/V’E graph in the 9-panel plot of Wasserman. There is currently no objective and standardised method for quantifying ventilatory irregularity.

The aim of this investigation is to develop a non-linear mathematical approach to objectify erratic breathing patterns based on the relationship between tidal volume (V’T) and minute ventilation (V’E) during cardiopulomnary excersise testing. Data from post-COVID patients will be compared with those of healthy, endurance-trained athletes as a reference group. In addition, the diagnostic accuracy of the developed method will be compared with a visual assessment by professionals.

In the long term, the procedure is intended to objectify the diagnosis of respiratory dysfunction in post-COVID patients and serve for future diagnostic and therapeutic approaches.

As part of this cross-sectional study, 35 healthy endurance athletes will be prospectively recruited and compared with 121 pseudonymised data sets from post-COVID patients from the previously completed EPILOC study (Ethics Committee approval S-846/2021).

Following written consent, the 35 newly enrolled endurance athletes will undergo a sports medicine examination. As part of the study, data from a cardiopulmonary exercise test (CPET) collected during routine clinical diagnostics will be used for scientific analysis. In particular, breath-by-breath data on minute ventilation (V'E) and tidal volume (V'T) will be recorded; from these, parameters of ventilatory irregularity will be calculated using a newly developed mathematical appooach. In addition, established exercise physiology parameters (including VO₂max and the V'E/V'CO₂ slope) are analysed.

The V'T/V'E diagrams are additionally assessed by highly qualified doctors to any pathological erratic breathing patterns. The agreement between visual assessment and the mathematical parameters is examined using ROC analyses. No further recruitment or additional data collection will take place amongst post-COVID patients.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
At least 6 hours per week, in at least 4 training sessions, of general basic training in swimming, running and/or cycling

VO₂max of ≥ 50 mL·min⁻¹·kg⁻¹ for men and ≥ 45 mL·min⁻¹·kg⁻¹ for women, taking into account an annual age-related decline of 1% from the age of 35

Ability to give consent and written consent to participate in the study
Exclusion criteria:
Known severe cardiovascular, metabolic, orthopaedic or other conditions that preclude intensive physical exertion

Acute illnesses or injuries at the time of the examination that preclude a stress test on a bicycle ergometer

A break in training of ≥ 2 weeks following a SARS-CoV-2 infection

A reduction in physical performance lasting ≥ 4 weeks following SARS-CoV-2 infection

Diagnosed chronic fatigue syndrome

If full exercise capacity is not achieved (respiratory exchange ratio of < 1.05), the data sets will be excluded from the statistical analysis
